extractedText: ☰ FAV0 July 10, 2026 · Friday OpenAI Releases GPT-5.6 Family: Sol, Terra, Luna Flagship Sol leads coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity, and science benchmarks at lower token cost. Terra balances performance and affordability. Luna delivers speed for high-volume tasks. GPT-5.6 family rolls out now in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API — OpenAI's most capable models yet. OpenAI officially launched the GPT-5.6 family on July 9, introducing three distinct models under the names Sol, Terra, and Luna. Sol is the flagship, engineered for long-horizon coding and agentic work that demands planning, tool use, and follow-through. On the long-term agentic benchmark, Sol scored 53.6, surpassing Claude Fable 5 at 40.5 — and at lower cost. Terra is positioned as the balanced workhorse, delivering performance competitive with GPT-5.5 at a reduced price point. Luna rounds out the trio as the fastest and most affordable model, optimized for well-defined, high-volume workloads. All three are available immediately in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, with pricing at $5/30, $2.5/15, and $1/6 per million input/output tokens respectively. Context windows extend to one million tokens with maximum output of 128k tokens. NVIDIA confirmed that GPT-5.6 was trained and runs on GB200 and GB300 NVL72 rack-scale systems. CEO Sam Altman called it "obviously the best model we have ever produced" and emphasized that the per-task dollar metrics represent a major step forward for enterprise customers concerned about AI costs. OpenAI president Greg Brockman praised Sol's performance in coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity, and science, noting that lower token costs make the model accessible to a wider range of applications. The release comes alongside a suite of product updates including the merger of Codex and ChatGPT into a unified desktop application, the launch of ChatGPT Work as a new agent experience, and a new Chrome extension with revamped in-app browser. Meta launched Muse Spark 1.1 with dramatically improved agentic, coding, and multimodal capabilities. The Meta Model API enters public beta. Meta Releases Muse Spark 1.1, Nears Frontier Performance Meta launched Muse Spark 1.1, a major upgrade from the original Muse Spark, matching GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8 on agent, coding, and multimodal benchmarks. The model ranks fourth on the overall Vals index and is the fastest model in the top ten. CEO Mark Zuckerberg personally announced the release, highlighting its competitiveness in agent and coding tasks. Meta researcher @hwchung27 noted that the API is "really, really cheap" and designed to open agentic intelligence to more people. Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang independently confirmed that the model rivals GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8 across many agentic evaluations. "The rate at which intelligence is getting cheaper still feels underrated," the Meta researcher added. Alongside the release, Meta opened a public beta for the new Meta Model API, giving developers direct access to Muse Spark 1.1. Codex and ChatGPT Merge into Unified Desktop App New coding workflows, Chrome extension, revamped in-app browser, and faster Computer Use powered by GPT-5.6. OpenAI merged the powerful coding agent Codex with ChatGPT Work into a single desktop application, now available on mobile, web, and desktop. OpenAI president Greg Brockman described ChatGPT Work as "an agent for your most ambitious work," usable across all platforms without needing a laptop left running. The unified app introduces new coding workflows, a Chrome extension, a revamped in-app browser, and faster Computer Use capabilities. The same agent experience powers both coding tasks and general knowledge work within a single interface. With nearly 9 million active builders, Ollama is positioning itself at the center of the open-source AI ecosystem. Co-founder Michael Chiang and Benchmark partner Peter Fenton appeared on CNBC to discuss the "post-frontier era" and open-source AI's breakout moment.
